data.cultural_impact: The name Amitraghna carries significant meaning in Hindu culture, representing a protector from enemies and a destroyer of evil forces. It is often associated with divine beings who possess the power to vanquish adversaries.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu philosophy, Amitraghna signifies the inner strength and courage to combat inner and outer negative influences. It reflects a deep spiritual resolve to overcome obstacles and cultivate an enlightened state of being, transcending beyond dualities, such as friendship and enmity.

historical_references.reference: The name Amitraghna is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata, in the context of the Pandava prince Bhima. Bhima, in one of his exploits, killed a demon named Hidimba in the forest of Kamyaka. Hidimba's brother Bhishma, the grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, was enraged by Bhima's act and cursed him to be afflicted by Amitraghna, a powerful and cruel demon. This demon tormented Bhima during his exile in the forest, until he was rescued and freed by the sage Vyasa.
historical_references.time_period: Late 4th century BCE to early 3rd century BCE

historical_references.reference: Amitraghna is also mentioned in the Jain texts, specifically in the works of Acharya Hemchandra, a 12th-century Jain scholar. Hemchandra refers to Amitraghna as a powerful Tirthankara, the 21st in the current cycle of 24 Tirthankaras. He is believed to have lived during the Avimechchha-vriddha-kalpa, a time period that is not clearly defined in historical records, but is traditionally believed to have occurred before the 2nd millennium BCE.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu name 'Amitraghna' is gaining popularity in modern contexts due to its association with peace, tranquility, and protection from negative energies. It is often used in the context of yogic practices, meditation, and New Age spirituality. On Instagram, there are numerous posts and stories featuring the name 'Amitraghna' in relation to yoga poses and calming images. On Facebook, there are groups and pages dedicated to the study and practice of Amitraghna mantras and rituals. On YouTube, there are videos explaining the significance of the name and how it can be used in meditation and other spiritual practices.

name_in_real_life.story: Lakshmi Amitraghna from Bali, Indonesia embodies the meaning of Amitraghna - "Slayer of Foes". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Amitraghna, meaning "the inexplicable sorrow destroyer," embodies the power to alleviate deep-rooted emotional pain and suffering. It symbolizes the inner strength to face and overcome adversities, ultimately leading to inner peace and tranquility.
